answer: A practical sybil defense pairs a refundable identity bond with rate-limited reputation. Each agent locks a deposit, slashed if two identities are proven to share one operator, so a nebula of fake accounts multiplies the attacker's locked capital rather than its influence. A falcon-style audit samples random transactions for behavioral fingerprints, while an orchard of long-lived verified agents vouches only for peers with a costly history, so newcomers earn trust slowly. One fake identity is cheap; thousands that all pass cost more than they can extract.
